producer_report.summary:
I wrote review 2 at docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-2.md and verified it passes the boundary wording scan. The verdict is approve with named changes: no blockers or majors, three minor findings and one nit. A table checks every review-1 finding (M1–M7, m1–m8, n1–n2) and the eight decisions against the design section each one cites. All hold. The review then runs the eight §9 checks. The three minors, with the design sections they cite:
- R2-m1: §2.1 item 4 lets a run start if the spend cap is only observed, which contradicts D64 decision 3.
- R2-m2: study.finding/1 has no field naming which elements or claims it covers, so two §5.4 rules can't be coded as written.
- R2-m3: a replay difference has no finding kind.

The nit is a miscount of evidence rules in Appendix A. I updated the design's status line and §9 to link review 2 and list those changes as pending, and added a CHANGELOG entry. No governance file or policy.rs was touched. The review avoids every banned word ("operators" included), and the word search found no matches. cargo test, fmt and clippy all pass.

One limit on the test evidence: the boundary test only reads git-tracked files, so it did not read the new file. The word search is what checked it."

checks_run.note: All suites pass, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where. That test reads only git-tracked files, so it did not read the new untracked review file; see the grep entry.

checks_run.command: Grep for every banned word and fragment from xtask/tests/policy.rs over docs/design
checks_run.note: Case-insensitive, whole words, same list as boundary_words and boundary_fragments, with the fragments rejoined. No matches in the new review or the edited design.

open_issues: Review 2 approves with named changes that this job did not apply to the design. R2-m1: §2.1 item 4 says a run does not start if the spend cap can be 'neither enforced nor observed', which conflicts with D64 decision 3. R2-m2: study.finding/1 has no subject field naming the element or claim ids, so 'Unexercised path' and 'Divergence unrecorded' cannot be coded as written. R2-m3: no finding kind covers a replay difference. R2-n1 is a wording fix to the count of evidence rules in Appendix A. The design's status line and §9 say these are answered before a build job is asked for.
Review 2 is by the same agent family as the producer and read the revised design and review 1 directly. Whether that meets the design's 'independent reviewer' standard is for the user to judge.
mistakes: Review 2's first draft had a muddled nit (R2-n1) about counting evidence rules. I corrected it before finishing. The pin rule is already one of review 1's six, so the eight rules are six plus two, not plus three.
learnings: The boundary test (athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where) scans git ls-files only, so a new untracked file passes cargo test whatever it contains. The banned list (xtask/tests/policy.rs boundary_words) covers: operator(s), opctl, ccr, sandbox(es/ed), lease(s), handoff(s) with or without a hyphen, and cloud/remote session(s). It matches whole words, case-insensitively.
Review 1 is the format model for a design review here: a verdict line, a header table, stable finding ids, a severity scale, one section per §9 check, and a list of what was read and run.
docs/decisions.md D64 exists and the CHANGELOG already had a line for the revised design.
desires: A way to make the boundary test see untracked files, or a supported command to scan a new file before Athena stages it.
